questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: More difficult than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder for several reasons. You cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare affects your vision. More tired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you must run the engine to operate a pump.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead of you:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
questions.explanation: Always watch the road ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: A vehicle with improper placards:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for hazardous materials cannot be driven, except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling restless. Staying in your lane is safe driving behavior, not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out, you should:

options.text: Move away and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away from the flames and wait for firefighters. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops between:
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops the flow of air.

questions.question: A distracted driver:
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice hazards on the road more slowly than focused drivers. Sometimes they do not notice hazards at all.

questions.question: Liquids expand:

options.text: At rates based on how fast the vehicle is moving.

questions.explanation: Liquids expand as temperature increases. Different liquids expand at different rates. You must leave extra space in the tank, called outage, for the liquid to expand. Know the outage requirements for your cargo.

questions.question: Front-to-back surge is usually very strong in which type of tank?
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks have nothing inside to slow down liquid movement. The liquid can surge back and forth easily.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the emergency line and service line shut-off valves. Listen for air escaping to make sure the air brakes work on all trailers. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When approaching a bridge or overpass, what should you do?

options.text: Trust that the posted clearance height is correct
Assume the posted clearance height may not be correct
Measure the height of the opening before going under it

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the posted clearance height may not be correct
questions.explanation: Do not trust posted height signs. The road may have been repaved or snow may be on the ground, making the actual height different. If you are unsure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: How should you drive a tank vehicle through curves?

options.text: Take curves faster than the posted speed limit
Take curves much slower than the posted speed limit
Use both lanes if there are two lanes of traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Take curves much slower than the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have a high center of gravity and can easily roll over. Drive well below the speed limit on curves to reduce this risk.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when going downhill?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle downhill, causing it to speed up.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver takes about 3/4 of a second to react. At 55 mph, you travel 61 feet during this time.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm or attack others
Driving a vehicle that is unsafe
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm or attack others
questions.explanation: Road rage means driving with the intent to harm another driver or damage their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving, which is selfish or pushy driving.

questions.question: What should you do to warn other drivers when slowing down?
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes before slowing down. This makes your brake lights flash, warning drivers behind you.

questions.question: What should you do if the brakes cannot build up pressure?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down as far as possible

questions.explanation: If your brakes are not building pressure, try shifting to a lower gear. You can also pump the brakes or use the emergency brake.
